descriptionChirho: A banner, standard, or ensign raised on a hill or pole as a rallying point for troops or peoples, or as a signal visible from afar (Isa 5:26, 11:10,12, 13:2, 18:3, 49:22, 62:10, Jer 4:6,21, 50:2, 51:12,27, Psa 60:4, Ezek 27:7).
A pole or staff set upright, on which something is displayed; used of the pole on which Moses set the bronze serpent (Num 21:8-9), and possibly a ship's mast (Isa 33:23).
A sign or warning signal raised as a visible reminder or admonition; used of an exemplary punishment that serves as a warning to others (Num 26:10, Isa 30:17).
